models_evaluated: Custom CNN bone age assessment algorithm (trained on RSNA Bone Age Challenge and Cheng-Hsin General Hospital images)

links.outcome: Radiologist bone age accuracy (MAD) with vs without AI assistance, and automation bias assessed
links.effect: MAD improved from 0.74 to 0.46 years with AI (p<0.001); >1 year error proportion 24.0% vs 8.4%; improved predictions 16.8% vs worsened 2.3%; less experienced radiologists prone to automation bias.
links.quote: The overall accuracy of senior, mid-level, and junior radiologists improved significantly with AI assistance than without AI assistance (MAD: 0.74 vs 0.46 years, p < 0.001; proportion of assessments for which MAD exceeded 1 year: 24.0% vs 8.4%, p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Effect of AI on radiologist performance in reader-study workflow versus standalone
links.effect: Radiologist MAD improved from 0.74 to 0.46 years with AI assistance (p<0.001); proportion >1 year error fell 24.0% to 8.4%.
links.quote: As illustrated in Fig. 5 , the radiologists’ assessment accuracy improved significantly ( p < 0.001) with AI assistance (MAD, 0.46 years) when compared with that without AI assistance (MAD, 0.74 years).

links.outcome: Automation bias and whether radiologists detected/rejected AI outputs
links.effect: Worsened predictions with AI in 2.3% vs improved 16.8%; junior radiologists accepted AI more readily; senior radiologists disagreed more (253 disagreements, 21.2%).
links.quote: Our study revealed that junior radiologists were more easily influenced by AI interpretations and generally accepted them.

models_evaluated: AI algorithm for bone age assessment

links.effect: Without vs with AI: MAD 0.74 vs 0.46 years; MAD>1 year 24.0% vs 8.4%; both p < 0.001.
links.quote: The overall accuracy of senior, mid-level, and junior radiologists improved significantly with AI assistance than without AI assistance (MAD: 0.74 vs 0.46 years, p < 0.001; proportion of assessments for which MAD exceeded 1 year: 24.0% vs 8.4%, p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Automation bias and AI disagreements by experience
links.effect: Worsened ≥1 y: 28 (2.3%) vs improved ≥1 y: 201 (16.8%); disagreements: S1/S2 65/65, M1/M2 23/55, J1/J2 18/27.
links.quote: Radiologists reading BAs were prone to automation bias when being supported by an AI algorithm, especially in less experienced radiologists.
